account: Today I have been keeping my appointments, though the morning grain inspection was unsuccessful because I could not find the miller. The baker and neighbour also said they had not seen the miller; I do not know why the miller is absent. Several townsfolk have repeated rumours about bridge or port changes affecting bakery deliveries, but neither the secretary nor baker has confirmed any changes. The baker told me freight delivered wheat last night and that the bread stall is well stocked, so I have no confirmed evidence of a grain shortage or disrupted access. The baker came to the office to ask about those rumours and offer bread for the hall, not to deliver correspondence. The secretary reported no new mail. I attended tea with the neighbour at the dockside cottage and have now returned to the office for my 16:30 appointment. The secretary is here, and the builder is waiting nearby holding a lantern. We have a confirmed appointment at 18:00 inside the great hall to inspect the lighting; the lantern seems consistent with that purpose, although I have not yet asked why the builder is here early. I intend to attend that inspection and return home at 19:00. Nothing I have directly observed establishes that the delivery rumours or the miller's absence are connected to the lighting inspection.
